# Multi-Registry Image Search Workflow

Implementation plan for adding a concurrent multi-registry search/browse capability triggered directly from the OCI Images tab (`tabImages`), replacing the old single-registry browser entirely.

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - **Removal of Registries Tab Browse**:
>   - The "Browse" feature will be removed from the Registries tab. Pressing `Enter` on the Registries tab will no longer open a browser.
>   - The OCI registry browser is now opened from the **Images tab** using the `b` shortcut.
> - **Authentication Integration**:
>   - For each registry selected in the search checklist, the browser will retrieve and use stored Docker credentials (from `docker login`, managed by `docker.GetStoredCreds()`) if `AuthEnabled` is true.
> - **Registry Filtering in Results**:
>   - Pressing `r` in the results table cycles the active registry filter (e.g. showing only `docker.io` tags, only a private registry's tags, or `All`).

## Open Questions

> [!NOTE]
> None. All design choices have been aligned with user feedback.

## Proposed Changes

### OCI Resources Components

We will repurpose the existing `registry_browser.go` and clean up the coordinator files to completely replace the single-registry browse workflow.

---

#### [MODIFY] [registry_browser.go](file:///c:/Users/anthoni/projects/gitlab/devdesk/internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go)
- Redefine `RegistryBrowser` to support multi-registry search and browse.
- **Form State**:
  - `repoInput textinput.Model`: text input for the image/repository name (e.g. `nginx`).
  - `registries []config.RegistryItem`: configured registries retrieved from context.

  - `focusedField int`: cursor index (0 = repo name, 1..N = registry checkboxes, N+1 = Search button).

  - `Up`/`Down`/`j`/`k` to navigate inputs, checklist checkboxes, and search button.
  - `Space` to toggle checkbox selection status.
  - `r` to cycle through the searched registries in the tags result table.

  - Form layout with checkbox indicators (`[x]` / `[ ]`) and submit button.
  - Results table with the new `Registry` column.

#### [MODIFY] [model.go](file:///c:/Users/anthoni/projects/gitlab/devdesk/internal/ui/oci_resources/model.go)
- Add new message definitions:
  - `MultiRegistryTagsLoadedMsg`: sent as each selected registry finishes querying tags.

- Delete unused single-registry message definitions if any.

#### [MODIFY] [commands.go](file:///c:/Users/anthoni/projects/gitlab/devdesk/internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go)

- Remove or deprecate single-registry fetch command functions.

J'ai lu l'implémentation. Voici l'état des lieux, puis les axes de design.

---

## Ce qui existe aujourd'hui

**Modèle de données** — `internal/config/config.go:58-80`

```go
type RegistryItem struct {
    URL, Username, Alias string
    AuthEnabled   bool
    ManagementURL string   // API du repo manager quand ≠ URL Docker
}
```

Liste **plate**, aucune notion de parent. Le mot de passe n'est jamais stocké (`docker login` → credential helper). Migration legacy `Registry.URL` → un `RegistryItem` unique.

**Les groupes existent, mais seulement en mémoire et seulement découverts**

- `internal/registrymgr/detector.go` : interface `Detector{CanHandle, DetectGroup}` + registre global. Une seule implémentation : `nexus.go`.
- Détection Nexus : `GET /service/rest/v1/repositories/{name}` (→ `type == "group"`), fallback `/repositories/{format}/group/{name}` (nécessite `nx-repository-admin`), puis retry anonyme. Les URLs de membres sont **fabriquées** (`host + /repository/ + memberName`), alias nettoyé de `-proxy|-hosted|-local`.
- La relation parent/enfant ne vit que dans `RegistryBrowser.entryGroups` / `browserRegistryEntry{ParentAlias, parentURL}` (`registry_browser.go:33-38`). **Rien n'est persisté.**

**Vue Registries** (`update.go:1449`) — table plate 5 colonnes : `URL | Username | Alias | Auth | Logged`. Le formulaire a 7 champs, dont `ManagementURL`. Aucun affichage de groupe.

**Browse** (touche `b` depuis l'onglet Images)

`newRegistryBrowser` lance `detectRegistryGroupCmd` pour **chaque** registre, **à chaque ouverture** → état bloquant `browserStateResolving` (spinner, N appels HTTP à 8s de timeout) avant même d'afficher le formulaire. Puis liste plate de checkboxes avec un groupement purement visuel (indentation + label parent), tout coché par défaut.

Auth au search (`registry_browser.go:381-404`) : `credURL = parentURL ?: entry.URL`, puis `docker.GetStoredCreds(credURL)`. **C'est le seul héritage implémenté** — et il fonctionne parce que Docker indexe les creds par hôte.

---

## Les trous, avant de parler design

| # | Problème | Où |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`AuthEnabled` est ignoré au browse et à la détection** — `GetStoredCreds` est appelé inconditionnellement. Un registre marqué « sans auth » enverra quand même les creds du host s'il y en a. | `registry_browser.go:393`, `commands.go:563` |
| 2 | Détection réseau systématique à chaque ouverture, sans cache ni refresh manuel. Latence + inutilisable offline. | `registry_browser.go:158-163` |
| 3 | Impossible de **déclarer** un groupe : uniquement de la découverte Nexus. Pas de groupe logique (« mes registres client-A »), pas de Harbor/Artifactory/GitLab. | modèle |
| 4 | `NexusDetector.CanHandle` retourne `true` dès que `ManagementURL != ""` → mono-vendor de fait. | `nexus.go:30-35` |
| 5 | Le filtre `r` des résultats cycle par URL de membre ; `registryFilterLabel()` cherche dans `m.registries` où les membres n'existent pas → affiche l'URL brute. Pas de filtre « par groupe ». | `registry_browser.go:485-533` |
| 6 | Sélection des registres non mémorisée : tout est recoché à chaque ouverture. | `finalizeEntries()` |
| 7 | En `browserStateResolving`, `esc` est ignoré → pas d'échappatoire si une détection ne revient pas. | `registry_browser.go:321` |

---

## Axes de design

### A. Modèle de données

Trois formes possibles :

**A1 — clé de groupement sur la liste plate** (`group: nexus-prod`). Migration triviale, mais le groupe n'a pas d'identité : pas d'URL pullable propre, pas de `ManagementURL`, pas de creds propres.

**A2 — deux listes** (`registries` + `registry_groups`). Le groupe devient un objet de première classe. Mais deux formulaires, deux tables, et un groupe Nexus *est* aussi un registre pullable — la séparation est artificielle.

**A3 — une liste, un discriminant, un pointeur parent** ← ma recommandation

```yaml
registries:
  - url: nexus.example.com/repository/docker-group
    alias: nexus
    kind: group
    provider: nexus
    management_url: https://nexus.example.com/repository/docker-group
    auth_mode: credentials
    username: svc-docker
  - url: nexus.example.com/repository/docker-proxy
    alias: docker-proxy
    parent: nexus.example.com/repository/docker-group
    auth_mode: inherit
```

Une seule table, un seul formulaire (les champs `parent`/`provider` n'apparaissent que selon `kind`), tri et filtre restent possibles, et un groupe reste pullable — ce qui colle au modèle Nexus réel.

**Question ouverte** : la clé parent est-elle l'URL (stable aujourd'hui, déjà l'identifiant partout dans le code) ou un `id`/slug ? L'URL casse le lien si on l'édite ; un slug demande une migration et un champ de plus dans le form.

### B. Auth — remplacer le booléen par un mode

`AuthEnabled bool` → `AuthMode` en champ cycle (Rule 132) : `anonymous | credentials | inherit`.

| Cas d'usage | Modélisation |
|---|---|
| Registre distant sans auth | `kind=registry, auth=anonymous` |
| Registre distant avec auth | `kind=registry, auth=credentials` |
| Groupe anonyme, membres anonymes | groupe `anonymous`, membres `inherit` |
| Groupe authentifié | groupe `credentials`, membres `inherit` |
| Groupe anonyme, un membre protégé | ce membre en `credentials` (override) |

Ça règle aussi le trou n°1 : `anonymous` doit **court-circuiter** `GetStoredCreds`, pas juste sauter le login.

⚠️ **Contrainte physique** : Docker indexe `~/.docker/config.json` **par hôte**, pas par chemin. Deux membres Nexus du même host partagent forcément le même login — `inherit` y est la seule réalité possible. L'override par membre n'a de sens que pour un groupe *logique* dont les membres sont sur des hôtes différents. À décider : est-ce qu'on veut supporter ce cas, ou est-ce qu'on assume « un groupe = un host » ?

### C. Découverte vs déclaration — où vivent les membres ?

Trois sources à réconcilier : découvert (API), manuel (l'utilisateur choisit un parent), mixte (découvert + exclusions).

**Option C1 — persister les membres découverts dans `config.yaml`.** La vue Registries devient la source de vérité éditable, le browser est instantané, ça marche offline. Mais on pollue un fichier déclaratif avec des données dérivées, et ça dérive du serveur.

**Option C2 — cache disque + TTL** dans `~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`, aligné sur le pattern `internal/cache` existant (ImageScanCache/WorkspaceScanCache, Rule 126). Config = ce que l'utilisateur déclare ; cache = ce qui a été découvert ; le browser fusionne. Refresh explicite via `ctrl+r` sur la ligne du groupe.

Je penche pour **C2** : c'est cohérent avec un pattern déjà en place dans le projet, ça garde le config propre, et ça donne un `ctrl+r` naturel. Colonne `Members` affichant le compte + `theme.TimeAgo(discovered_at)` pour rendre la fraîcheur visible.

### D. Affichage de la hiérarchie dans la vue Registries

- **D1 — colonne `Group`** sur la table plate. Le plus simple, compatible FilterBar (Rule 136) et tri.
- **D2 — indentation** (parent puis membres indentés), comme le browser fait déjà. Lisible, mais tri et filtre cassent la hiérarchie.
- **D3 — drill-down `←/→`** (Rule 111) : niveau 1 = groupes + registres standalone, `→` entre dans le groupe. C'est le pattern déjà utilisé par gitlab-explorer, et cohérent avec les tabs breadcrumb (Rule 123).

D3 est le plus aligné avec les conventions du projet ; D2 est plus rapide à lire quand on a 5 registres. Ton appel.

Colonnes proposées : `Alias | URL | Kind | Auth | Login | Members`.

### E. Browse — sélection et filtrage

- Formulaire alimenté par config + cache → **plus de détection bloquante**, affichage immédiat.
- Checkbox sur le **groupe** avec état tri-state (all / partial / none) qui propage aux membres. Aujourd'hui seuls les membres sont cochables.
- Persister la sélection par contexte.
- Filtre résultats : cycler `groupe → membres du groupe → all`, et résoudre les alias de membres (corrige le trou n°5).

**Question de fond à trancher** : interroger le **groupe** (1 requête, union des tags, provenance perdue) ou les **membres** (N requêtes, on sait que ce tag vient de `docker-hosted`) ? Le code actuel a implicitement choisi les membres — c'est le bon choix pour la provenance, mais il faut le documenter et éviter d'interroger les deux (doublons garantis).

### F. Extensibilité des detectors

Avec un `kind: group` explicite, ajouter `provider: nexus|harbor|artifactory|gitlab|generic` en champ cycle du formulaire est plus fiable que le sniffing actuel. `CanHandle` devient un simple match sur `provider`, avec un detector générique en dernier recours.

---

## Ce sur quoi j'aimerais ton avis

1. **Clé parent** : URL ou slug ?
2. **Groupe cross-host** : on le supporte (override auth par membre) ou on assume « un groupe = un host » ?
3. **Membres découverts** : config (C1) ou cache (C2) ?
4. **Vue Registries** : drill-down (D3) ou arbre indenté (D2) ?
5. Est-ce qu'un **groupe purement logique** (agrégat de registres sans repo manager derrière — juste un dossier de rangement) fait partie du besoin, ou uniquement les groupes réels type Nexus ?

1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-03
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	**None open.** D1–D11 are all fixed; §1.1 records what each was and why the
15	chosen fix was the right one.
16	
17	The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not
18	because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
19	so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
20	decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).
21	
22	### 1.1 Fixed
23	
24	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
25	phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.
26	
27	The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
28	the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
29	was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
30	The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`
31	without documenting it at all.
32	
33	The workspaces view had it too, found in phase 3: `n` and `Enter` documented
34	where the bindings are `ctrl+n` and `enter`, `/` undocumented, and the same
35	stale "Press [n]" in its empty state.
36	
37	`explorer` made it four in a row, though only just: every key was documented
38	except `/`. The check caught it on its first run.
39	
40	`security` broke the streak — its help documents every key its header
41	advertises, across all four states. So the drift was not universal after all;
42	three of the five views that carried it were the ones where a binding had been
43	renamed by Rule 111 and the help was not updated with it.
44	
45	All four are fixed, and every view in `internal/ui` now asserts that each key
46	`GetShortcuts()` advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would
47	have caught the drift when it was introduced.
48	
49	**The explorer acted on a different row than the one highlighted.** Found in
50	phase 3, and the most serious defect the coverage work has turned up.
51	
52	`handleKeyMsg` resolved the cursor against `sortedItems(currentItems())` — the
53	unfiltered list — while the table was built from the filtered one. With a filter
54	active the two indices disagree, so `ctrl+d`, `p`, `→` and `ctrl+w` all acted on
55	whatever happened to sit at that index in the *unfiltered* list. Filtering to a
56	single project and pressing `ctrl+d` scheduled a different group for deletion.
57	`GetShortcuts` had it too, so even the advertised `ctrl+w` keyed off the wrong
58	node.
59	
60	Both now go through `visibleItems()`, the single list `updateTableRows` builds
61	from. Pinned by `TestActionsResolveTheRowTheUserCanSee`, which filters to a row
62	that sits at a different index in each list — the fixtures were chosen so the
63	two cannot coincide.
64	
65	**A stranded cursor in the workspaces table.** `bubbles/table.SetRows` does not
66	clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks. Drilling into a directory with
67	fewer entries — or narrowing the filter — left the cursor past the end: nothing
68	highlighted, and `enter`, `ctrl+d`, `r` and `ctrl+s` all silently did nothing
69	until the user pressed an arrow key. `updateTableData` now clamps.
70	
71	The containers view avoids this by calling `GotoTop()` after every filter
72	change; workspaces had no equivalent. **`explorer` had it too**, and only on the
73	filter path — its drill-down was already safe because it calls `GotoTop()`.
74	Fixed the same way.
75	
76	**Footer messages with no timer.** `explorer.handleDeleteComplete` set
77	`footerError` and returned `nil`, so a failed delete left "Delete failed — check
78	logs" on screen until something else overwrote it. Rule 128 caps footer messages
79	at three seconds, and the same file's `BrowserOpenedMsg` handler already did it
80	correctly. Now returns `clearFooterErrorCmd()`.
81	
82	The security view had it worse: **Rule 128 was not honoured anywhere in it.**
83	`statusMessage` was set in three places — "Added x to .gitleaksignore", "Failed
84	to ignore secret", "No references available" — and there was no clear timer in
85	the package at all, so whichever happened last stayed on screen until a tab
86	switch happened to reset it. `clearStatusCmd` / `clearStatusMsg` added and all
87	three wired, pinned by `TestFooterMessagesExpire`.
88	
89	**D7** (`extractTarGz` kept parent references in archive paths), **D2** (the
90	"permanent delete" checkbox was documented as locked but was not) and **D5** (an
91	unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`) were fixed together — three small,
92	independent defects with no shared code.
93	
94	`extractTarGz` now routes every member name through `sanitizeArchivePath`, which
95	normalises the separators and rejects anything resolving outside the root.
96	Cleaning happens *after* the leading separator is stripped, not before:
97	`path.Clean("/../x")` returns `"/x"`, which would have absorbed the traversal
98	silently instead of exposing it. Traversal that resolves back inside the root
99	(`templates/../README.md`) is kept, normalised. Backslashes are folded to `/`
100	first, so `..\..\etc\passwd` cannot pass as an ordinary filename on a tar reader
101	that treats it as one.
102	
103	The delete modal carries a `locked` flag, set only by
104	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent`. Rather than merely making the toggle a no-op,
105	navigation skips the checkbox entirely (`minFocus()` / `cycleFocus()`) and the
106	line renders dimmed: a focusable control that ignores every key is more
107	confusing than one that is plainly not there.
108	
109	The `CreationForm` clamp was deleted and replaced by a comment recording why it
110	cannot fire, so it is not reintroduced defensively. A test pins the invariant it
111	was guarding.
112	
113	Both self-annulling tests became real assertions:
114	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable` →
115	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsLocked` (plus navigation and
116	confirmation cases), and `TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys` →
117	`TestExtractTarGzRejectsParentTraversal` (table-driven over five escape shapes)
118	alongside `TestExtractTarGzNormalisesContainedTraversal`.
119	
120	**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
121	looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
122	fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.
123	
124	Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
125	`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
126	the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
127	terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
128	ones.
129	
130	A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
131	in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
132	Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
133	gone.
134	
135	A **sixth site** closed the family out, in the last package of phase 3:
136	`parseVersion` in `internal/ui/security` truncated its fallback with
137	`result[:15]`. Version strings are ASCII in practice, so this was the
138	lowest-risk of the six — but it is the same pattern, and it is now
139	`theme.TruncateWidth`. Grepping for `[:` on strings across `internal/ui` now
140	returns nothing but slice indexing.
141	
142	The same function had a second defect: it scanned for the version number by
143	taking the first whitespace-separated token starting with `v`, so
144	`gitleaks version 8.18.2` reported its version as **"version"**. A leading `v`
145	now only counts when a digit follows it.
146	
147	A **fifth site** turned up during the phase 3 tests: `firstOutputLine` in
148	`internal/ui/netdiag` sliced `line[:maxLen-3]` to fill the Output column of the
149	results table, so any diagnostic whose first line contained a multibyte rune
150	could be cut in half and bleed across the rows below (Rule 122). Now
151	`theme.TruncateWidth`, pinned by `TestFirstOutputLineKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`.
152	Worth grepping for `[:` on strings when the remaining phases land.
153	
154	The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
155	(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
156	`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).
157	
158	One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
159	`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
160	so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
161	theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
162	
163	**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
164	planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.
165	
166	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
167	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
168	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
169	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
170	same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
171	won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
172	after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
173	strips the path before the helper is ever called.
174	
175	**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
176	the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
177	change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
178	`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.
179	
180	Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
181	path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
182	contexts anyway.
183	
184	Two smaller defects went with it:
185	
186	- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
187	  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
188	  hang indefinitely.
189	- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
190	  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
191	  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
192	  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.
193	
194	`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
195	than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
196	`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
197	common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
198	`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
199	`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.
200	
201	### 1.2 The five parked defects
202	
203	D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 were each recorded rather than fixed on discovery,
204	because each changed something the user already saw. They were decided together
205	and fixed in one pass. Three of the five had a test written to fail *on the
206	fix*, and all three did.
207	
208	**D4 — `tab` navigated the delete confirmation.** Rule 135 reserves `tab` for
209	switching tabs and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively; the modal
210	had it exactly inverted, cycling on `tab` and clamping on `↑ / ↓`. `↑ / ↓` now
211	cycle, which is what keeps every control reachable in one direction, and the
212	`tab` cases are gone. The explorer no longer advertises "tab Navigate" while the
213	modal is open, and `↑↓` is not advertised in its place — Rule 138 calls it
214	obvious. The permanent variant still skips its locked checkbox, so cycling there
215	toggles between the two buttons.
216	
217	**D8 — write-only CRUD flags.** `creating`, `editing` and `confirming` were
218	assigned in five places and read in none, and `ComponentFormCancelledMsg` — the
219	only thing that would have reset two of them — could never be sent. Deleted, all
220	of it. Nothing else changed: the phase 2 tests had deliberately asserted on
221	`componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags, which is what made
222	this safe a phase later.
223	
224	**D9 — the containers list opened Z→A.** `New()` set neither `sortColumn` nor
225	`sortAsc`, so both took their zero value. Both are now set explicitly, so the
226	default is stated rather than inherited. `TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending`
227	became `TestDefaultSortIsNameAscending`, and the cycle test walks forward from
228	ascending. The `loadedModel` helper still sets the sort itself even though it
229	now matches the constructor: those tests should say which order they rely on.
230	
231	**D10 — a registry failure was invisible.** `renderTemplateList` returned early
232	when the field was unfocused and the warning sat below that return, so a form
233	opened after the OCI registry failed offered a Template field reading "none"
234	with nothing to distinguish "the registry is down" from "there are no

241	`theme.StatusErrorStyle` it returned for HIGH. The palette moved to
242	`theme.SeverityTextStyle`, next to the `TableStylesForSeverity` it draws from,
243	and the view delegates (Rule 102). An unrecognised severity now falls back to
244	the info colour rather than to `DimStyle`, so it is still legible.

246	The pattern worth keeping: when a defect is recorded rather than fixed, write
247	the test **inverted** — asserting the current behaviour and saying so. D9, D10
248	and D11 each had one, and each failed the moment the fix landed, which is how

293	`app` remain.

295	`internal/gitlab` needed no seam: every function takes a `*gitlabclient.Client`
296	built from a base URL, so an `httptest` server standing in for the API covers
297	the whole package. `Clone` is exercised against a throwaway local repository
298	rather than mocked, and skips when no `git` binary is on `PATH`.

300	Phase 2, complete:
301	
302	| Package | Before | Now |
303	|---|---|---|
304	| `internal/ui/status` | 0 % | **93.9 %** |
305	| `internal/ui/status/components` | 0 % | **93.2 %** |

319	Three constraints the phase surfaced, worth knowing before phases 3–5:
320	
321	- **Colour has to be forced to test styling.** Under `go test` lipgloss detects
322	  no TTY, falls back to the Ascii profile and strips every escape sequence — so
323	  any assertion about colour passes whatever the code does. `containers` calls
324	  `lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor)` for the tests that need it and
325	  restores it afterwards; that is what makes the Rule 122 check (no escape
326	  sequences in `table.Row` cells) real rather than vacuous. Verified by styling
327	  a cell on purpose and watching the test fail. `termenv` moved to a direct
328	  dependency for this.

330	  asserted by looking for the error-selection escape sequence in the rendered

333	  total order or the expected sequences are ambiguous.

335	Phase 3, in progress:
336	
337	| Package | Before | Now |
338	|---|---|---|
339	| `internal/ui/netdiag` | 15.9 % | **86.1 %** |
340	| `internal/ui/workspaces` | 0 % | **81.3 %** |
341	| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer` | 0 % | **91.5 %** |
342	| `internal/ui/security` | 0 % | **83.7 %** |

344	**Phase 3 is complete.** The three-step order held on all four: surface pass
345	58.8 % / 60.3 % / 58.1 % / 52.9 %, split with the figure unchanged to the
346	statement every time, completion pass to 86.1 % / 81.3 % / 91.5 % / 83.7 %.
347	
348	`workspaces` added one technique worth reusing: its filesystem commands
349	(`createWorkspace`, `deleteEntry`, `renameEntry`, `loadEntries`, `enrichEntry`)
350	are **executed** rather than asserted on identity, against `t.TempDir()` and a
351	throwaway git repository. That is what proves the branch, remote and dirty-tree
352	counters are read correctly; a stub would only prove the stub works. It skips
353	when `git` is not on `PATH`, like `internal/gitlab` does. Only the Docker- and
354	desktop-backed commands are left alone.
355	
356	`explorer` extended that to the API layer, which is why it reaches 91.5 % —
357	higher than either of the others despite having the largest untestable-looking
358	surface. The rule that emerged: **execute the command whenever the dependency
359	can be stood up locally**, and only fall back to asserting on model state when
360	it cannot.
361	
362	| Dependency | Treatment |
363	|---|---|
364	| GitLab API | executed against `httptest` — the SDK takes a base URL |
365	| OCI registry | executed against `httptest` |
366	| git | executed against a seeded repository, skipped without `git` on `PATH` |
367	| Desktop browser | not executed; the guard branches are driven, the launch is not |

369	The pull tests are the clearest case: the "GitLab host" is a local directory
370	holding seeded repositories, so `recursivePull` really clones and really writes
371	the directory tree. That is what proves the tree mirrors the group hierarchy,
372	that an existing checkout is skipped rather than clobbered, and that a group
373	whose children were never browsed is fetched mid-pull. `cloneURL` was extracted
374	from `pullProject` to make the SSH and HTTPS URL shapes assertable — `gitlab.Clone`

384	Its most worthwhile tests are not about the state machine at all: they are about
385	`extractMeaningfulLines`, which reduces a wall of Trivy and Gitleaks stderr to
386	the one line that explains a failure. What it *discards* — INFO lines, progress
387	bars, the doubled `Fatal error / run error:` wrapping — is the whole feature,

389	stops a novel log format leaving the user with nothing.

391	Two handlers are deliberately left uncovered in `containers`: `s` and `S` call
392	`detectShell`, which runs `docker exec` synchronously *inside* `Update`. The
393	tests drive those keys only in states that return before reaching it. The same
394	shape appears in `status.reloadConfigAndCheck`, which calls `config.Load()` from
395	`Update`. Neither is a Rule 110 violation — nothing mutates the model from a
396	`Cmd` — but I/O in `Update` blocks the event loop and is untestable without a
397	seam. Worth a look when phase 5 gets to the router.
398	
399	`internal/credentials` needed no seam either. `git credential` is steerable
400	through the environment, so the tests redirect `HOME`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and
401	`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` at a temporary directory and run the real binary against a
402	throwaway `store` helper — nothing reaches the developer's keychain. Running the
403	real git is what surfaced the context-isolation defect recorded in §1.1; a stub
404	would have frozen the broken behaviour instead. The 2 s timeout is covered by
405	installing a credential helper that sleeps.
406	
407	### Files over the 800-line ceiling
408	
409	The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Three still exceed it,
410	all outside the views phase 3 covered:
411	
412	| File | Lines |
413	|---|---|
414	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
415	| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
416	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |
417	
418	`internal/ui/security/model.go` (1991 lines, the largest file in the project)
419	was split into `update.go`, `form.go`, `scan.go`, `findings.go`, `details.go`,
420	`view.go`, `warnings.go`, `header.go` and `messages.go`; the largest is 299 and
421	`model.go` itself is 245. `warnings.go` is the one worth noticing: the
422	scan-error parser is pure string handling with no dependency on the model at
423	all, and pulling it out of a 2000-line file is what made it obvious it deserved
424	tests of its own.
425	
426	`internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` (1114 lines) was split into `validation.go`,
427	`update.go`, `run.go`, `view.go` and `header.go`; the largest is now 314 lines
428	and `model.go` itself is 172. `topology_model.go` stays at 752 — under the
429	ceiling, and its parsers and renderer belong together.
430	
431	`internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` (1299 lines) was split into `messages.go`,
432	`table.go`, `entry.go`, `actions.go` and `update.go`; the largest is 450 and
433	`model.go` itself is 129. `entry.go` is the one worth noticing: the pure and
434	filesystem-only helpers now sit together instead of at the bottom of a
435	1300-line model, which is what made them straightforward to cover.
436	
437	`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` (1402 lines) was split into `update.go`,
438	`table.go`, `navigation.go`, `pull.go`, `create.go`, `delete.go`, `api.go` and
439	`messages.go`; the largest is 227 and `model.go` itself is 206. `api.go` is the
440	one worth noticing: gathering every GitLab call into one file is what made the
441	`httptest` pass straightforward — the routes to fake are visible in one place
442	rather than scattered through a 1400-line model.
443	
444	`internal/docker/client.go` (1176 lines — the 1069 recorded earlier was stale)
445	was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,
446	`volumes.go`, `registry.go`, `launch.go`, `system.go` and `parse.go`; the largest
447	is now 269 lines. The former `network.go` became `ports.go`, since it reports the
448	host's listening sockets via `ss` rather than Docker networks — the name was
449	free for the `docker network` family.
450	
451	This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
452	tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
453	Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
454	7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.
455	
456	**The order settled on for phase 3 is: surface tests, then split, then complete
457	coverage** — per package, so each split has a net under it without the tests
458	being written against a layout that is about to change. It held across all four
459	packages, with the coverage figure unchanged to the statement every time
460	(58.8 %, 60.3 %, 58.1 %, 52.9 %), including on the 1991-line `security/model.go`.
461	Use it for phases 4 and 5. The discipline that makes it work is
462	asserting on behaviour rather than on internals — no test named a file, and the
463	only ones that reach into the model do so for state the view has no other way to
464	expose.
465	
466	### Race detector cannot run locally
467	
468	`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
469	it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
470	concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.
471	
472	**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
473	every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
474	run reported no data race across all 17 packages.
475	
476	That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
477	tests actually execute, and coverage is 55.3 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
478	paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
479	this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.
480	Phase 2 puts the first full view state machine under the detector.
481	
482	Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
483	avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.

486	
487	## 3. Planned features
488	
489	Carried over from `todo.md`, except §3.7.
490	
491	### 3.1 Network diagnostics
492	
493	- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
494	  redirections to the host machine.
495	
496	### 3.2 Interactive security remediation
497	
498	- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
499	  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
500	- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
501	  directly into the Workspace view.
502	
503	### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser
504	
505	- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
506	  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
507	  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
508	    the Docker daemon).
509	  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
510	    downloading the whole image.
511	  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
512	  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
513	- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
514	  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".
515	
516	### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers
517	
518	- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
519	  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
520	- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
521	  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.
522	
523	### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)
524	
525	- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
526	  for every container in the selected project.
527	- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).
528	
529	### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context
530	
531	Support GitHub as well as GitLab, with **exactly one backend active per
532	configuration context**. A context targets one forge; switching forge means
533	switching context.
534	
535	Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
536	not a chosen design.
537	
538	#### What is coupled to GitLab today
539	
540	| Surface | Size |
541	|---|---|
542	| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
543	| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |
544	
545	The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
546	(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
547	rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
548	interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.
549	
550	Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
551	clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
552	and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
553	`shared.GitLabStats`.
554	
555	#### Model mismatches to settle before coding
556	
557	These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
558	promise.
559	
560	- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
561	  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
562	  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
563	  backend declares.
564	- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
565	  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
566	  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
567	  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there. The `locked`
568	  flag added in §1.1 is the hook for that: a GitHub backend would set it and
569	  leave the box out of reach, as the already-scheduled GitLab case does.
570	- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
571	  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
572	  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
573	  limits and semantics.
574	- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
575	  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
576	  applies either way.
577	
578	#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs
579	
580	Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
581	package needs a seam.
582	
583	Arguments for the CLIs:
584	
585	- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
586	  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
587	  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
588	- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
589	  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
590	- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.
591	
592	Arguments against:
593	
594	- **Per-context isolation conflicts with how these tools store auth.** Both keep
595	  global per-host state (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`). DevDesk contexts want
596	  *different tokens for the same host*. Driving `gh auth switch` from the TUI
597	  would mutate the user's global CLI state — the exact mistake avoided in §1.1 by
598	  scoping `credential.useHttpPath` to the invocation. The clean route is
599	  `GH_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` per invocation, but then DevDesk still owns the
600	  tokens and the main benefit is gone.
601	- **Two more hard dependencies.** Today DevDesk needs `git`, and `docker` only
602	  for the features that use it. Requiring `gh` and `glab` for the core forge
603	  feature is a real setup-friction regression.
604	- **Cost per call.** A process spawn per request, against a reused HTTP
605	  connection today. The dashboard alone issues five calls, and the explorer
606	  paginates.
607	- **Testability regresses.** `internal/gitlab` reaches 100 % with no seam,
608	  because the SDK takes a base URL that an `httptest` server can stand in for.
609	  Shelling out would put it back in the position `internal/docker` was in, needing
610	  a manufactured seam — and stubbed CLI output encodes assumptions about the tool
611	  rather than testing against it.
612	
613	**Current recommendation:** keep Go SDKs (go-gitlab, go-github) for the API
614	surface, and use the CLIs only as an *optional* token source — when a context has
615	no token, offer to read one from `gh auth token --hostname <host>` or
616	`glab auth status`. That takes the convenience without the coupling. Recorded as
617	a recommendation, not a decision.
618	
619	#### Sketch of the work
620	
621	1. Define a `forge` abstraction from what the code actually consumes: current
622	   user, namespace tree, create/delete namespace and repository, initial commit,
623	   dashboard counters, clone URL.
624	2. Replace `shared.State.GitLabClient` with that interface. This is the change
625	   the other 65 call sites follow from.
626	3. Generalise `GitLabConfig` into a per-context forge config carrying a
627	   `type: gitlab | github` discriminator, and migrate existing config files.
628	4. Implement the GitLab backend by moving the existing code behind the
629	   interface — behaviour-preserving, and covered by the tests added in #7.
630	5. Implement the GitHub backend.
631	6. Rename the views and commands, keeping `gla` / `gle` as aliases so muscle
632	   memory survives.
633	
634	Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own: they are a refactor of working code with
635	tests already in place, and they are what makes step 5 tractable.
636	
637	### 3.7 Command mode from inside a text field — **done**
638	
639	`alt+:` now opens the command line from anywhere, including a focused text
640	input. A bare `:` keeps its old, conditional behaviour, so muscle memory
641	survives.
642	
643	The problem: `handleKeyMsg` routed `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which
644	asked the view whether it was in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it
645	was, forwarded the keystroke to the active input. Command mode was therefore
646	unreachable from any form, filter box or search field — most of the application.
647	
648	The security view is the case that settles it. `InEditMode()` is true there for
649	the target path, Trivy server and Gitleaks config fields, and the Trivy server
650	placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954` — the field has to accept **two**
651	colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:` to the input is not a bug; it is
652	the only correct behaviour, which is precisely why `:` cannot be the
653	authoritative key. The only way in was to move focus to a control that takes no
654	text and press `:` there, so reachability depended on which widget was focused
655	and nothing said so.
656	
657	It was worse in `StateScanning`, `StateResults`, `StateDetails` and while a
658	confirm modal is open: `InEditMode()` is true and there is no field to move
659	focus to. `:` was forwarded to the view, which has no `case` for it — no view in
660	the application handles `:` itself — and dropped silently.
661	
662	#### Why `alt+`, not `ctrl+`
663	
664	`ctrl+:` cannot be made to work, and this is the note that should stop anyone
665	reintroducing it. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing bits, which only covers
666	ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F). `:` is 0x3A: Ctrl+: sends a plain `:` or
667	nothing. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty keyboard protocol or
668	xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements neither. A
669	`case "ctrl+:"` would be dead code.
670	
671	Alt has no such limit — a terminal sends ESC then the key, and bubbletea reports
672	that as the key carrying `Alt`. The alternative considered was a free
673	`ctrl+<letter>` (`b g l p t u v x z` are unused; `ctrl+i m j h [` are Tab, Enter,
674	LF, Backspace and Esc and must be left alone), which is marginally more portable
675	but loses the `:` in the gesture.
676	
677	#### What shipped
678	
679	- `altCommandModeKey` is handled in `handleKeyMsg` **before** the `InEditMode()`
680	  fork, so no view can claim it. The router sees every `tea.KeyMsg` first, which
681	  is what makes the binding unconditional.
682	- `enterCommandMode()` extracted; `maybeEnterInCommandMode` now only answers the
683	  bare `:`.
684	- `testutil.Key` understands an `alt+` prefix, building the key with the `Alt`
685	  modifier rather than the five literal runes `alt+:`. Both round-trip through
686	  `String()`, but only one is the message the application actually receives.
687	- Every `GetShortcuts()` and `GetHelpContent()` advertising `:` now advertises
688	  `alt+:` (Rules 114, 130, 137). The dashboard's Navigation help section carries
689	  the nuance in prose, so the other eight sites stay one line each.
690	- The header still renders `:` as the inactive prompt: it is the command line's
691	  visual marker, not a key legend, and `:` remains valid whenever no field has
692	  focus.
693	
694	Two things the ripple list got wrong, corrected here: `app_test.go:30` is a
695	layout fixture for `buildShortcutLines`, not an assertion about the binding, so
696	it was left alone. And `CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` was not merely
697	made redundant by this change — **it was already dead code**. The router only
698	consulted it when `InEditMode()` was true, and netdiag's implementation returns
699	true only on the topology tab, where `InEditMode()` is unconditionally false. It
700	could never fire. Deleted, along with its one implementation;
701	`TestCommandModeOnTheTopologyTab` became
702	`TestTheTopologyTabNeverBlocksCommandMode` and records why.
703	
704	---
705	
706	## 4. Existing plans
707	
708	Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is referenced directly from the old
709	`todo.md` and is still outstanding:
710	
711	- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
712	  — Docker-layer platform portability.

# DevDesk Backlog

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-03

Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
rather than carried over.

---

## 1. Known defects

**None open.** D1–D11 are all fixed; §1.1 records what each was and why the
chosen fix was the right one.

The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not
because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).

### 1.1 Fixed

**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.

The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`
without documenting it at all.

The workspaces view had it too, found in phase 3: `n` and `Enter` documented
where the bindings are `ctrl+n` and `enter`, `/` undocumented, and the same
stale "Press [n]" in its empty state.

`explorer` made it four in a row, though only just: every key was documented
except `/`. The check caught it on its first run.

`security` broke the streak — its help documents every key its header
advertises, across all four states. So the drift was not universal after all;
three of the five views that carried it were the ones where a binding had been
renamed by Rule 111 and the help was not updated with it.

All four are fixed, and every view in `internal/ui` now asserts that each key
`GetShortcuts()` advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would
have caught the drift when it was introduced.

**The explorer acted on a different row than the one highlighted.** Found in
phase 3, and the most serious defect the coverage work has turned up.

`handleKeyMsg` resolved the cursor against `sortedItems(currentItems())` — the
unfiltered list — while the table was built from the filtered one. With a filter
active the two indices disagree, so `ctrl+d`, `p`, `→` and `ctrl+w` all acted on
whatever happened to sit at that index in the *unfiltered* list. Filtering to a
single project and pressing `ctrl+d` scheduled a different group for deletion.
`GetShortcuts` had it too, so even the advertised `ctrl+w` keyed off the wrong
node.

Both now go through `visibleItems()`, the single list `updateTableRows` builds
from. Pinned by `TestActionsResolveTheRowTheUserCanSee`, which filters to a row
that sits at a different index in each list — the fixtures were chosen so the
two cannot coincide.

**A stranded cursor in the workspaces table.** `bubbles/table.SetRows` does not
clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks. Drilling into a directory with
fewer entries — or narrowing the filter — left the cursor past the end: nothing

**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.

The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
strips the path before the helper is ever called.

**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.

Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
contexts anyway.

### Race detector cannot run locally

`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.

**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
run reported no data race across all 17 packages.

That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
tests actually execute, and coverage is 55.3 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.
Phase 2 puts the first full view state machine under the detector.

Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.

### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context

Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
not a chosen design.

#### What is coupled to GitLab today

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |

The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.

Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
`shared.GitLabStats`.

#### Model mismatches to settle before coding

These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
promise.

- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
  backend declares.
- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there. The `locked`
  flag added in §1.1 is the hook for that: a GitHub backend would set it and
  leave the box out of reach, as the already-scheduled GitLab case does.
- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
  limits and semantics.
- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
  applies either way.

#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs

Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
package needs a seam.

Arguments for the CLIs:

- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.

Arguments against:

- **Per-context isolation conflicts with how these tools store auth.** Both keep
  global per-host state (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`). DevDesk contexts want
  *different tokens for the same host*. Driving `gh auth switch` from the TUI
  would mutate the user's global CLI state — the exact mistake avoided in §1.1 by
  scoping `credential.useHttpPath` to the invocation. The clean route is
  `GH_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` per invocation, but then DevDesk still owns the
  tokens and the main benefit is gone.
- **Two more hard dependencies.** Today DevDesk needs `git`, and `docker` only
  for the features that use it. Requiring `gh` and `glab` for the core forge
  feature is a real setup-friction regression.
- **Cost per call.** A process spawn per request, against a reused HTTP
  connection today. The dashboard alone issues five calls, and the explorer
  paginates.
- **Testability regresses.** `internal/gitlab` reaches 100 % with no seam,
  because the SDK takes a base URL that an `httptest` server can stand in for.
  Shelling out would put it back in the position `internal/docker` was in, needing
  a manufactured seam — and stubbed CLI output encodes assumptions about the tool

### 3.8 Docker registry groups

Two shapes have to be supported: a remote registry with or without
authentication, and a **group** fronting several remote registries, itself
reachable anonymously or not. The second is the one the current model cannot
express.

Not started. The decisions below are settled; one is not, and is marked as such.

#### What the current code does

| Concern | Today | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Parent/child relation | in memory only, for the lifetime of one browser session | `registry_browser.go:33` (`browserRegistryEntry`) |
| Group discovery | Nexus REST, re-run on **every** browser open, 8 s timeout each, behind a blocking spinner | `registry_browser.go:158`, `registrymgr/nexus.go` |
| Member URLs | synthesised as `host + /repository/<memberName>`, alias stripped of `-proxy`/`-hosted`/`-local` | `nexus.go:111`, `nexus.go:200` |
| Credential inheritance | member searches use the **parent's** URL as the `~/.docker/config.json` lookup key | `registry_browser.go:381` |
| Registries tab | flat table, no indication a group was ever found | `update.go:1449` |
| Result filter (`r`) | cycles member URLs; no group level | `registry_browser.go:485` |

`RegistryConfig.Registries` is a flat `[]RegistryItem` and carries no parent
field. Nothing about a group survives closing the browser: it is rediscovered,
over the network, next time.

The credential inheritance is the one piece that already behaves correctly, and
the reason it does is the same reason the open decision below is hard.

#### Settled

| Ref | Decision |
|---|---|
| A | **One list, one discriminator, one parent pointer** — `kind: registry \| group` plus `parent` on `RegistryItem`. Two parallel lists and a recursive `Children` tree were both rejected. |
| 1 | The parent is referenced by **slug**, not by URL. |
| 3 | Discovered members live in a **disk cache**, not in `config.yaml`. |
| 4 | The Registries tab gets **drill-down** navigation (`←` / `→`), not an indented tree and not a `Group` column. |
| 5 | **No purely logical groups.** A group always corresponds to a real repository-manager group. |
| F | `provider` is a **declared field**, not sniffed from the URL. |

**A — one list.** A Nexus group *is* a pullable registry as well as a container,
so splitting `registries` and `registry_groups` would have duplicated the form,
the table and the credential handling to model a distinction the server does not
make. A single list with a discriminator keeps one table, one form (fields shown
per `kind`), and leaves sorting and filtering intact.

**1 — slug over URL.** The URL is today's de facto identifier and is threaded
through `registryLoginStatus`, the scan cache keys and the message types, which
is exactly why it is the wrong thing to hang a parent link on: editing a group's
URL would silently orphan its members. The slug replaces the URL **only as the
parent link and the cache key** — everything Docker-facing stays keyed on the
URL, because that is what Docker itself is keyed on. Existing configs migrate by
deriving a slug from the alias, falling back to the URL host; uniqueness has to
be enforced at load, and the form needs to reject a collision rather than accept
a config that will not round-trip.

**3 — cache, not config.** Discovered members are derived data with a server as
their source of truth, and `config.yaml` is what the user declares. Putting them
in the cache mirrors `ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` (Rule 126) rather
than inventing a fourth persistence shape:
`~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`, keyed by group slug, refreshed
explicitly with `ctrl+r` on a group row. The browser then reads config plus
cache and opens instantly and offline, which is what removes D13's blocking
state rather than papering over it. A `Members` column showing the count and
`theme.TimeAgo(discovered_at)` (Rule 127) is what keeps staleness visible —
without it, a silently stale cache is worse than the current re-detection.

**4 — drill-down.** Level 1 lists groups and standalone registries; `→` enters a
group and lists its members; `←` goes back, with a breadcrumb below the table
(Rules 111, 123). The indented-tree alternative reads faster at five registries
but breaks the moment the table is sorted or the FilterBar (Rule 136) narrows
it, and drill-down is already the pattern `gitlab-explorer` uses. Proposed
columns: `Alias | URL | Kind | Auth | Login | Members`.

**5 — no logical groups.** Grouping unrelated registries under a user-invented
name was considered and dropped: it has no server to discover from, no shared
credential to inherit, and no group URL to pull through, so it would be a
display-only concept carrying the weight of a real one. If the need for
arbitrary grouping appears later it is a saved-selection feature in the browser,
not a change to the registry model.

**F — declared provider.** `NexusDetector.CanHandle` currently returns true
whenever `ManagementURL` is non-empty (`nexus.go:31`), which makes that field do
double duty as an implicit "this is Nexus" flag and makes the detector list
effectively single-vendor. A `provider` field on the group — `nexus`, `harbor`,
`artifactory`, `gitlab`, `generic` — turns `CanHandle` into a match on a
declared value, with the generic detector last. It is a cycle field in the form
(Rule 132) and it is what makes a second implementation possible without
guessing.

#### Open: how far credential inheritance goes

The concrete case: a Nexus group **with** authentication fronting eight Nexus
proxies. Browsing the proxy that points at `dhi.io` has to query the *proxy's*
URL while authenticating with the *group's* credentials.

That much the code already does — `submitSearch` sets
`credURL = parentURL ?: entry.URL` — and the reason it works is worth stating
explicitly, because it constrains everything else:

> **`docker login` takes a registry host, not a path.** `~/.docker/config.json`
> is keyed on `host[:port]`, so the group and all eight proxies share one single
> credential entry, because they share `nexus.example.com`.

Three consequences:

- `inherit` is not a convenience for path-based groups, it is the **only** thing
  the credential store can represent. Every member of such a group authenticates
  identically whether the model says so or not.
- A per-member `credentials` override is **not storable today**. It would need
  DevDesk to own a credential store keyed by slug, which puts passwords back in
  DevDesk's custody — something `RegistryItem` avoids by construction (it has no
  password field; §1.1 records how badly the last credential-storage bug went).
- What a member *can* usefully override is **`anonymous`**: do not send the
  group's credentials to this one. That is representable, costs nothing, and is
  the safety valve — and it is the same mechanism D12 needs.

Proposed, pending the discussion: replace `AuthEnabled bool` with an `AuthMode`
cycle field where a group is `anonymous | credentials` and a member is
`inherit | anonymous`. The four cases in scope then map cleanly:

| Case | Group | Member |
|---|---|---|
| Remote registry, no auth | — | `kind: registry`, `anonymous` |
| Remote registry, auth | — | `kind: registry`, `credentials` |
| Group with auth, 8 proxies (the case above) | `credentials` | `inherit` |
| Anonymous group | `anonymous` | `inherit` |

What still needs deciding is whether a member-level `credentials` is worth
supporting at all. It only becomes meaningful for a group whose members are on
different hosts, which decision 5 has just ruled out of the model — so the
current reading is that it should not exist, and that a genuine need for it is a
separate decision about who stores the password.

**Adjacent question to settle before the model is frozen: browse and pull may
not share a URL.** Path-based Nexus access answers the registry API at
`/repository/<name>/v2/...`, which is what `registryAPIURL` builds and what the
tag search relies on. Whether `docker pull` accepts the same path-form reference
depends on the deployment — a dedicated HTTP connector port per repository is
the older Nexus arrangement, path routing needs a reverse proxy in front. If
they differ, a member needs a third URL alongside `url` and `management_url`,
and `multiImageName` (`registry_browser.go:685`) is building an unpullable
reference today. **This should be checked against the actual Nexus instance**
rather than reasoned about; it is one `docker pull` away from being answered.

#### Sequencing

This lands in `internal/ui/oci_resources`, which is **phase 4** of the coverage
plan (§2, ~1 995 statements, pending) and holds two of the three files still
over the 800-line ceiling — including `registry_browser.go` at 822, which this
feature grows.

Do it in the phase-3 order that held on all four large views: **surface tests,
then split, then complete coverage**, and only then the feature. Writing the
group model into an 822-line file with no tests under it repeats the mistake
that order exists to prevent.

#### Sketch of the work

1. Add `slug`, `kind`, `parent` and `provider` to `RegistryItem`; migrate
   existing configs and enforce slug uniqueness at load.
2. Replace `AuthEnabled` with `AuthMode`, and make **both** registry-facing
   paths honour it — this is D12, and it is the step that gives `anonymous`
   meaning.
3. Add `internal/cache/registrygroups.go` alongside the two existing caches;
   move discovery behind it and give the Registries tab an explicit refresh.
4. Turn `CanHandle` into a match on the declared `provider`, with a generic
   detector last.
5. Drill-down in the Registries tab, with the `Members` column and breadcrumb.
6. Rework the browser to read config plus cache: no resolving state (D13),
   group-level checkboxes with a tri-state, a group level in the result filter
   and resolvable member labels (D14), and a remembered selection per context.

Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own — they are what make the group model
expressible — and step 6 is the one that needs step 3 finished first.

the table and the credential handling to model a distinction the server does not

per `kind`), and leaves sorting and filtering intact.

through `registryLoginStatus`, the scan cache keys and the message types, which
is exactly why it is the wrong thing to hang a parent link on: editing a group's
URL would silently orphan its members. The slug replaces the URL **only as the
parent link and the cache key** — everything Docker-facing stays keyed on the
URL, because that is what Docker itself is keyed on. Existing configs migrate by
deriving a slug from the alias, falling back to the URL host; uniqueness has to
be enforced at load, and the form needs to reject a collision rather than accept
a config that will not round-trip.

their source of truth, and `config.yaml` is what the user declares. Putting them
in the cache mirrors `ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` (Rule 126) rather
than inventing a fourth persistence shape:

explicitly with `ctrl+r` on a group row. The browser then reads config plus
cache and opens instantly and offline, which is what removes D13's blocking
state rather than papering over it. A `Members` column showing the count and
`theme.TimeAgo(discovered_at)` (Rule 127) is what keeps staleness visible —
without it, a silently stale cache is worse than the current re-detection.

group and lists its members; `←` goes back, with a breadcrumb below the table
(Rules 111, 123). The indented-tree alternative reads faster at five registries
but breaks the moment the table is sorted or the FilterBar (Rule 136) narrows
it, and drill-down is already the pattern `gitlab-explorer` uses. Proposed
columns: `Alias | URL | Kind | Auth | Login | Members`.

**5 — no logical groups.** Grouping unrelated registries under a user-invented
name was considered and dropped: it has no server to discover from, no shared
credential to inherit, and no group URL to pull through, so it would be a
display-only concept carrying the weight of a real one. If the need for
arbitrary grouping appears later it is a saved-selection feature in the browser,
not a change to the registry model.

**F — declared provider.** `NexusDetector.CanHandle` currently returns true
whenever `ManagementURL` is non-empty (`nexus.go:31`), which makes that field do
double duty as an implicit "this is Nexus" flag and makes the detector list
effectively single-vendor. A `provider` field on the group — `nexus`, `harbor`,
`artifactory`, `gitlab`, `generic` — turns `CanHandle` into a match on a
declared value, with the generic detector last. It is a cycle field in the form
(Rule 132) and it is what makes a second implementation possible without
guessing.

The concrete case: a Nexus group **with** authentication fronting eight Nexus
proxies. Browsing the proxy that points at `dhi.io` has to query the *proxy's*
URL while authenticating with the *group's* credentials.

That much the code already does — `submitSearch` sets
`credURL = parentURL ?: entry.URL` — and the reason it works is worth stating
explicitly, because it constrains everything else:

> **`docker login` takes a registry host, not a path.** `~/.docker/config.json`
> is keyed on `host[:port]`, so the group and all eight proxies share one single
> credential entry, because they share `nexus.example.com`.

Three consequences:

- `inherit` is not a convenience for path-based groups, it is the **only** thing
  the credential store can represent. Every member of such a group authenticates
  identically whether the model says so or not.
- A per-member `credentials` override is **not storable today**. It would need
  DevDesk to own a credential store keyed by slug, which puts passwords back in
  DevDesk's custody — something `RegistryItem` avoids by construction (it has no
  password field; §1.1 records how badly the last credential-storage bug went).
- What a member *can* usefully override is **`anonymous`**: do not send the
  group's credentials to this one. That is representable, costs nothing, and is
  the safety valve — and it is the same mechanism D12 needs.

| Remote registry, no auth | — | `kind: registry`, `anonymous` |
| Remote registry, auth | — | `kind: registry`, `credentials` |
| Group with auth, 8 proxies (the case above) | `credentials` | `inherit` |
| Anonymous group | `anonymous` | `inherit` |

supporting at all. It only becomes meaningful for a group whose members are on
different hosts, which decision 5 has just ruled out of the model — so the
current reading is that it should not exist, and that a genuine need for it is a
separate decision about who stores the password.

not share a URL.** Path-based Nexus access answers the registry API at

depends on the deployment — a dedicated HTTP connector port per repository is
the older Nexus arrangement, path routing needs a reverse proxy in front. If
they differ, a member needs a third URL alongside `url` and `management_url`,
and `multiImageName` (`registry_browser.go:685`) is building an unpullable
reference today. **This should be checked against the actual Nexus instance**
rather than reasoned about; it is one `docker pull` away from being answered.

This lands in `internal/ui/oci_resources`, which is **phase 4** of the coverage
plan (§2, ~1 995 statements, pending) and holds two of the three files still
over the 800-line ceiling — including `registry_browser.go` at 822, which this
feature grows.

Do it in the phase-3 order that held on all four large views: **surface tests,
then split, then complete coverage**, and only then the feature. Writing the
group model into an 822-line file with no tests under it repeats the mistake
that order exists to prevent.

1. Add `slug`, `kind`, `parent` and `provider` to `RegistryItem`; migrate
   existing configs and enforce slug uniqueness at load.
2. Replace `AuthEnabled` with `AuthMode`, and make **both** registry-facing

3. Add `internal/cache/registrygroups.go` alongside the two existing caches;
   move discovery behind it and give the Registries tab an explicit refresh.
4. Turn `CanHandle` into a match on the declared `provider`, with a generic
   detector last.
5. Drill-down in the Registries tab, with the `Members` column and breadcrumb.
6. Rework the browser to read config plus cache: no resolving state (D13),
   group-level checkboxes with a tri-state, a group level in the result filter
   and resolvable member labels (D14), and a remembered selection per context.

Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own — they are what make the group model
expressible — and step 6 is the one that needs step 3 finished first.

Backlog updated — `docs/backlog.md`, two sections, no code touched.

**§1.3 Known defects — open (new)**

The review turned up three real defects, so §1's "None open" claim is no longer true and I corrected it:

- **D12** — `AuthEnabled` has no effect on browse or discovery. Both `submitSearch` and `detectRegistryGroupCmd` call `GetStoredCreds` unconditionally. Since Docker keys credentials by host, a registry marked "no auth" on a Nexus instance you've logged into *will* receive those credentials.
- **D13** — `esc` is ignored during `browserStateResolving`, so the browser is unresponsive for ~8 s on every open.
- **D14** — the result filter shows a raw synthesised URL for group members, because `registryFilterLabel()` searches a list they aren't in.

All three are recorded as fix-*with* §3.8 rather than ahead of it, since it rewrites the code path each one lives in.

**§3.8 Docker registry groups (new)**

Settled decisions recorded with the reasoning: one list + `kind`/`parent` discriminator (A), slug as parent key (1), disk cache for discovered members (3), drill-down navigation (4), no logical groups (5), declared `provider` (F). Plus a sequencing note — this package is coverage phase 4 and holds `registry_browser.go` at 822 lines, so surface tests → split → coverage → feature, per the order that held across phase 3.

**On point 2** — your concrete case did more than illustrate the problem, it mostly answers it. The reason the group's auth already works for the proxy's URL is that `docker login` takes a *host*, not a path: the group and all eight proxies are one entry in `~/.docker/config.json` because they're all `nexus.example.com`. So `inherit` isn't a convenience there, it's the only thing the credential store can represent — and a per-member `credentials` override isn't storable at all without DevDesk owning passwords again.

That leaves the enum as `anonymous | credentials` for a group and `inherit | anonymous` for a member, with `anonymous` doubling as the fix for D12. I recorded that as proposed-pending-discussion, not settled.

One thing I flagged as needing a check rather than a decision: **browse and pull may not share a URL.** The tag search hits `/repository/<name>/v2/...`, but whether `docker pull` accepts that same path form depends on how your Nexus is fronted (per-repo connector port vs reverse-proxy path routing). If they differ, members need a third URL and `multiImageName` is currently building a reference you can't pull. One `docker pull nexus.../repository/dhi-proxy/<image>:<tag>` against your instance settles it — worth doing before the model is frozen.
